Seven kinds of Great People join your empire over the game: Prophets, Scientists, Engineers, Merchants, Artists, Generals and Admirals. Each kind has its own points, earned every turn by buildings and wonders (Shrines and Temples for Prophets, Libraries and Universities for Scientists, Workshops and Factories for Engineers, Markets and Banks for Merchants, Amphitheaters and Museums for Artists, Barracks and Military Academies for Generals, Lighthouses and Harbors for Admirals; many wonders add points too). When the points reach the cost, the Great Person appears in your capital as a unit; the cost rises with every one you recruit. From half way you can recruit early with Devotion or Gold (Empire panel). The Inchibils are the wild people of the world: not an empire, not a Free city, nobody to talk to. Their camps (🏕️) sit in the wilderness and periodically release raiders that attack nearby units and settlements. Move a military unit onto a camp to disperse it for Gold (a big reward card tells you when you do). The raiders grow stronger as the world advances through the eras. Free cities, by contrast, are real single-city powers with a leader you can build Ties with.
